gallery.title: File:Sierra Nevada aerial.jpg
gallery.artist: Jeffrey Pang from Pittsburgh, PA, USA
gallery.description: North-northwest view of the Mills Creek cirque (center) in the Sierra National Forest near the midpoint of the Sierra Crest, which extends along the cirque's southeast corner (right) at Mounts Abbot and Mills northward from La Salle Lake (bottom, partially shadowed), the image's centerline is through the south side of the cirque between Mounts Hilgard (left, casting shadow w/ sunlit streak) and Gabb (right of centerline), then north of the cirque along the Sierra Crest's Red and White and Red Slate mountains (right of centerline).  The crest extends northwest to Mammoth Crest and Mammoth Mountain and then west of Mono Lake (top, blue) in the north, e.g., across Tioga Pass west of the Wheeler Crest.  Between the cirque and Mono Lake is Crowley Lake (white, right of centerline).

gallery.title: File:BishopTuff.jpg
gallery.description: Rocks from the Bishop Tuff, an ignimbrite tuff from Owens River Gorge, California.  On the left, a rock from the latter stages of the eruption and the top of the deposit; note large grey, oval pumice fragments.  On the right, a rock from the earlier part of the eruption and the bottom of the deposit; note dark, flat fiamme (squished pumice) and apparent increase in phenocrysts, though the compression that caused the fiamme most likely compressed the matrix of the tuff, increasing the apparent abundance of crystals, with respect to the matrix.

gallery.filename: Alabama Hills and Mt Whitney Range, Sierra Nevada 6-16 (27943280305).jpg
gallery.title: File:Alabama Hills and Mt Whitney Range, Sierra Nevada 6-16 (27943280305).jpg
gallery.artist: Don Graham from Redlands, CA, USA - God bless it!
gallery.description:
(1 in a multiple picture album)
The volcanic landscape in the foreground is called The Alabama Hills within which can be found Movie Flats. This was a place were many of the old Gene Autry and Roy Rogers Westerns were filmed.

In the background is the part of the Sierra Nevada where Mt. Whitney, the highest point in the contiguous United States is located. Many folks see the high peak in the center of the picture and guess that it is Mt. Whitney. It is not. That is Mt. Russell. Whitney is hiding a bit behind he. Look for the saddle on the left side of the picture. Mt. Whitney is behind that and set back.

gallery.title: File:"Galactic Kaleidoscope" (8583832479).jpg
gallery.description:
I travelled about 2.5 hours from the bay area to the foothills of the Sierra Nevada Mountains nearly 45 miles outside of Yosemite National Park searching for cosmic light and the galactic center of the Milky way. I had a vision of the bright center of our galaxy traversing over the high sierra mountain ranges sharing its colorful beauty with earth. When i arrived onsite, the moon was just setting and a light fog was moving through concealing the starlight i sought out for. I set up and considered my trip may have been in vain, thankfully, a few moments later as i moved my eyes from the camera viewfinder, the constellations Sagittarius and Scorpius came into brilliant view over the horizon. After reviewing my shots from the back of the camera i noticed the color and immense detail shown inside the milky way, it was like a nocturnal kaleidoscope bringing life to the sky. it was a beautiful experience, im happy to share this image
_Image Detail_
Shutter 382 seconds
14mm focal length
Aperture F2.8
ISO 3200
Sony Alpha a390 DSLR
Rokinon 14mm F2.8 ultrawide lens
tripod

I processed this image in a fashion that was done in a style paying respect to a photographer and friend of mine named Jack Fusco
His style of shooting the night sky inspired me to capture scenes like these. Check him out on flickr***
